f.title: Austrian PV decisions apply in Liechtenstein for recognised products
f.statement: Liechtenstein applies the decisions of the competent Austrian authority for the marketing authorisations and registrations covered by the Agreement, in particular decisions on the SmPC, labelling and package leaflet, the classification of the medicinal product and pharmacovigilance.
f.clause: Art. 4(1) Administrative measures of Austrian authorities
f.applicability: Human medicinal products authorised or registered by Austria in the mutual recognition or decentralised procedure and automatically recognised in Liechtenstein under Art. 2(1)

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder of a medicinal product authorised in Austria (MRP/DCP) and automatically recognised in Liechtenstein
rows.quote: Liechtenstein wendet die Bescheide der zuständigen österreichischen Behörde im Rahmen der von diesem Abkommen umfassten Zulassungen bzw. Registrierungen von Arzneimitteln an. Insbesondere betrifft dies die Entscheidungen hinsichtlich der Vorgaben zur Fachinformation, Kennzeichnung und Gebrauchsinformation, zur Einstufung des Arzneimittels sowie zur Pharmakovigilanz.
rows.location: Art. 4(1) Administrative measures of Austrian authorities
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the consolidated text (version 01.12.2016); quote proves the statement. Bilingual check: independent re-translation agrees with quote_en; German 'sind ... zu übermitteln' = shall; indicative present tense in a treaty provision read as binding. Double-check: statement adds nothing beyond the quote. Company relevance: Austrian PV decisions bind the product in Liechtenstein without a separate Liechtenstein decision.
rows.quote_en: Liechtenstein applies the decisions of the competent Austrian authority within the framework of the authorisations or registrations of medicinal products covered by this Agreement. This concerns in particular the decisions regarding the requirements on the summary of product characteristics, labelling and package leaflet, the classification of the medicinal product and pharmacovigilance.

f.title: Contact the Liechtenstein authority for RMP measures needing national implementation
f.statement: Pharmacovigilance systems and risk management plans are assessed by Austria in the authorisation procedure. Where measures proposed in risk management plans are subject to country-specific rules or require national implementation (for example dispensing status or distribution), Austria refers the applicant to the Liechtenstein medicines authority as the competent contact for Liechtenstein.
f.clause: Art. 5(1) Cooperation in pharmacovigilance: PV systems and RMPs
f.applicability: Human medicinal products authorised or registered by Austria in the mutual recognition or decentralised procedure and automatically recognised in Liechtenstein under Art. 2(1)
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Local PV interfaces

rows.quote:
Begutachtung von Pharmakovigilanz-Systemen und Risk-Management-
Plänen: Die Begutachtung wird im Rahmen des Zulassungsverfahrens von Österreich durchgeführt. Das Ergebnis ist Bestandteil des Assessment-Reports. Werden im Rahmen von Risk-Management-
Plänen Massnahmen vorgeschlagen, die landesspezifischen Regelungen unterliegen oder nationale Umsetzungen erfordern (z. B. Abgabestatus, Distribution), verweist Österreich den Antragsteller auf die liechtensteinische Arzneimittelbehörde als die für Liechtenstein zuständige Ansprechpartnerin.
rows.location: Art. 5(1) Cooperation in pharmacovigilance: PV systems and RMPs
rows.review_note: Review: the treaty describes what the Austrian authority does (refers the applicant/MAH to the Liechtenstein authority); the statement keeps that wording. The practical company duty (address the Liechtenstein authority for Liechtenstein-specific measures) follows from it but is not a modal obligation in the text. Double-check: held at 80 because the level rests on the indicative, not an explicit modal.
rows.quote_en: Assessment of pharmacovigilance systems and risk management plans: the assessment is carried out by Austria within the authorisation procedure. The result forms part of the assessment report. Where measures are proposed within risk management plans that are subject to country-specific rules or require national implementation (e.g. dispensing status, distribution), Austria refers the applicant to the Liechtenstein medicines authority as the competent contact for Liechtenstein.

f.title: Submit PSURs to the Austrian BASG (transitional, until the Directive 2010/84 date)
f.statement: Marketing authorisation holders submit periodic safety update reports (PSURs) to the Austrian Federal Office for Safety in Health Care (BASG) up to the date referred to in Article 2(7) of Directive 2010/84/EU. Assessment is carried out by Austria unless a single assessment under Art. 107e of Directive 2001/83/EC takes place; any resulting measures are communicated to Liechtenstein.
f.clause: Art. 5(2) Cooperation in pharmacovigilance: PSUR assessment
f.applicability: Human medicinal products authorised or registered by Austria in the mutual recognition or decentralised procedure and automatically recognised in Liechtenstein under Art. 2(1)
f.exceptions: Single EU assessment under Art. 107e Directive 2001/83/EC

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder of a medicinal product authorised in Austria (MRP/DCP) and automatically recognised in Liechtenstein
rows.deadline: Until the date referred to in Art. 2(7) of Directive 2010/84/EU
rows.quote: PSURs werden von den Zulassungsinhabern bis zu dem in Art. 2 Abs. 7 der Richtlinie 2010/84/EU genannten Zeitpunkt beim Bundesamt für Sicherheit im Gesundheitswesen eingereicht.
rows.location: Art. 5(2) Cooperation in pharmacovigilance: PSUR assessment
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the consolidated text (version 01.12.2016); quote proves the statement. Bilingual check: independent re-translation agrees with quote_en; German 'sind ... zu übermitteln' = shall; indicative present tense in a treaty provision read as binding. Double-check: statement adds nothing beyond the quote. The end date is not stated as a calendar date in the text (it is the date in Art. 2(7) of Directive 2010/84/EU), so no deadline_rule.
rows.quote_en: PSURs are submitted by the marketing authorisation holders to the Federal Office for Safety in Health Care up to the date referred to in Art. 2(7) of Directive 2010/84/EU.

f.title: Keep submitting PSURs to BASG for generics, well-established use products and THMPs
f.statement: PSURs for authorisations under Art. 10(1) and Art. 10a of Directive 2001/83/EC and for registered traditional herbal medicinal products continue to be submitted to the Austrian Federal Office for Safety in Health Care (BASG) after the date referred to in Art. 2(7) of Directive 2010/84/EU.
f.clause: Art. 5(2) Cooperation in pharmacovigilance: PSUR assessment
f.applicability: Products recognised under the Agreement that are authorised under Art. 10(1) (generics) or Art. 10a (well-established use) of Directive 2001/83/EC, and registered traditional herbal medicinal products

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder of a medicinal product authorised in Austria (MRP/DCP) and automatically recognised in Liechtenstein
rows.quote: PSURs für eine Zulassung nach Art. 10 Abs. 1 und Art. 10a der RL 2001/83/EG sowie für registrierte traditionelle pflanzliche Arzneispezialitäten werden auch danach beim Bundesamt für Sicherheit im Gesundheitswesen eingereicht.
rows.location: Art. 5(2) Cooperation in pharmacovigilance: PSUR assessment
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the consolidated text (version 01.12.2016); quote proves the statement. Bilingual check: independent re-translation agrees with quote_en; German 'sind ... zu übermitteln' = shall; indicative present tense in a treaty provision read as binding. Double-check: statement adds nothing beyond the quote.
rows.quote_en: PSURs for an authorisation under Art. 10(1) and Art. 10a of Directive 2001/83/EC and for registered traditional herbal medicinal specialities are also submitted thereafter to the Federal Office for Safety in Health Care.

f.title: Send reports of adverse reactions occurring outside the EEA directly to EudraVigilance
f.statement: In line with the Liechtenstein medicines authority notice "Reporting of Adverse Reactions" of 31 August 2004 and the BASG "Information on Electronic Reporting for Marketing Authorisation Holders" of 29 January 2007, each in its current version, reports of adverse reactions occurring outside the European Economic Area must be transmitted by the marketing authorisation holder directly to EudraVigilance.
f.clause: Art. 5(3) Cooperation in pharmacovigilance: individual case reports
f.applicability: Human medicinal products authorised or registered by Austria in the mutual recognition or decentralised procedure and automatically recognised in Liechtenstein under Art. 2(1); adverse reactions occurring outside the EEA
f.exceptions: Reports from clinical trials under Directive 2001/20/EC or Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 are outside the Agreement.
f.processes: Submission operations; Case processing & follow-up; E2B / transmission

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder of a medicinal product authorised in Austria (MRP/DCP) and automatically recognised in Liechtenstein
rows.quote: Einzelfallmeldungen: Gemäss Bekanntmachung der liechtensteinischen Arzneimittelbehörde zum "Reporting of Adverse Reactions" vom 31. August 2004 sowie der "Information des Bundesamtes für Sicherheit im Gesundheitswesen über Electronic Reporting für Zulassungsinhaber" vom 29. Januar 2007 in der jeweils aktuellen Version sind ausserhalb des Europäischen Wirtschaftsraums auftretende Nebenwirkungsmeldungen durch den Zulassungsinhaber direkt an EudraVigilance zu übermitteln.
rows.location: Art. 5(3) Cooperation in pharmacovigilance: individual case reports
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the consolidated text (version 01.12.2016); quote proves the statement. Bilingual check: independent re-translation agrees with quote_en; German 'sind ... zu übermitteln' = shall; indicative present tense in a treaty provision read as binding. Double-check: statement adds nothing beyond the quote. No time limit is stated in this Agreement (the referenced notices govern it), so no deadline_rule.
rows.quote_en: Individual case reports: in accordance with the notice of the Liechtenstein medicines authority on "Reporting of Adverse Reactions" of 31 August 2004 and the "Information of the Federal Office for Safety in Health Care on Electronic Reporting for Marketing Authorisation Holders" of 29 January 2007, each in its current version, reports of adverse reactions occurring outside the European Economic Area are to be transmitted by the marketing authorisation holder directly to EudraVigilance.

f.title: Report adverse reactions occurring in Liechtenstein electronically to EudraVigilance
f.statement: Adverse reactions occurring in Liechtenstein are reported by the marketing authorisation holder, in accordance with the Liechtenstein medicines authority notice "Reporting of Adverse Reactions" of 31 August 2004, by direct electronic transmission to EudraVigilance.
f.clause: Art. 5(3) Cooperation in pharmacovigilance: individual case reports
f.applicability: Human medicinal products authorised or registered by Austria in the mutual recognition or decentralised procedure and automatically recognised in Liechtenstein under Art. 2(1); adverse reactions occurring in Liechtenstein
f.exceptions: Reports from clinical trials under Directive 2001/20/EC or Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 are outside the Agreement.
f.processes: Submission operations; Case processing & follow-up; E2B / transmission

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder of a medicinal product authorised in Austria (MRP/DCP) and automatically recognised in Liechtenstein
rows.quote: Die Meldung von in Liechtenstein auftretenden Nebenwirkungen durch den Zulassungsinhaber erfolgt gemäss der Bekanntmachung der liechtensteinischen Arzneimittelbehörde zum "Reporting of Adverse Reactions" vom 31. August 2004 durch direkte elektronische Übermittlung an EudraVigilance.
rows.location: Art. 5(3) Cooperation in pharmacovigilance: individual case reports
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the consolidated text (version 01.12.2016); quote proves the statement. Bilingual check: independent re-translation agrees with quote_en; German 'sind ... zu übermitteln' = shall; indicative present tense in a treaty provision read as binding. Double-check: statement adds nothing beyond the quote.
rows.quote_en: Adverse reactions occurring in Liechtenstein are reported by the marketing authorisation holder in accordance with the notice of the Liechtenstein medicines authority on "Reporting of Adverse Reactions" of 31 August 2004 by direct electronic transmission to EudraVigilance.

f.title: MAHs not ready for electronic reporting: send Liechtenstein ADRs on paper to the LI authority
f.statement: Marketing authorisation holders that are not yet ready for electronic reporting report adverse reactions occurring in Liechtenstein on paper to the Liechtenstein medicines authority until an electronic reporting system is implemented; forwarding to Austria and further processing follow the arrangements for reports from healthcare professionals (forwarded to BASG within seven calendar days; BASG assesses and submits to EudraVigilance).
f.clause: Art. 5(3) Cooperation in pharmacovigilance: individual case reports
f.applicability: Human medicinal products authorised or registered by Austria in the mutual recognition or decentralised procedure and automatically recognised in Liechtenstein under Art. 2(1); adverse reactions occurring in Liechtenstein
f.processes: Submission operations; Case processing & follow-up; Local PV interfaces

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder not yet ready for electronic reporting
rows.deadline: Until implementation of an electronic reporting system
rows.quote: Zulassungsinhaber, die für die elektronische Meldung noch nicht bereit sind, melden in Liechtenstein auftretende Nebenwirkungen bis zur Implementierung eines elektronischen Meldesystems in Papierform an die liechtensteinische Arzneimittelbehörde. Die Weiterleitung an Österreich und die weitere Bearbeitung erfolgen in Analogie zu den Meldungen von Angehörigen der Gesundheitsberufe.
rows.location: Art. 5(3) Cooperation in pharmacovigilance: individual case reports
rows.review_note: Review: checked against the consolidated text (version 01.12.2016); quote proves the statement. Bilingual check: independent re-translation agrees with quote_en; German 'sind ... zu übermitteln' = shall; indicative present tense in a treaty provision read as binding. Double-check: statement adds nothing beyond the quote. The parenthesis on forwarding times summarises the authority-side arrangements stated earlier in Art. 5(3) for healthcare professional reports; they are not MAH deadlines.
rows.quote_en: Marketing authorisation holders that are not yet ready for electronic reporting report adverse reactions occurring in Liechtenstein in paper form to the Liechtenstein medicines authority until an electronic reporting system is implemented. Forwarding to Austria and further processing take place by analogy with reports from members of the health professions.

f.title: Planned DHPC for a recognised product: contact the Liechtenstein authority
f.statement: Where the sending of a "Dear Health Care Provider Letter" is planned for a medicinal product authorised or registered under the Agreement, Austria refers the marketing authorisation holder to the Liechtenstein medicines authority as the competent contact for Liechtenstein.
f.clause: Art. 5(4) Cooperation in pharmacovigilance: information for users
f.applicability: Human medicinal products authorised or registered by Austria in the mutual recognition or decentralised procedure and automatically recognised in Liechtenstein under Art. 2(1)

dates.title: Liechtenstein-Austria agreement on automatic recognition of Austrian MRP/DCP authorisations: enters into force
dates.scope: Human and veterinary medicinal products authorised or registered by Austria in MRP/DCP and automatically recognised in Liechtenstein, and their MAHs
dates.timing_note: Concluded in Vaduz on 31 May 2010; published 16 November 2010. The captured text is the consolidated version of 01.12.2016 (Art. 4(1), Art. 5 and Art. 8(3) amended by LGBl. 2016 Nr. 387); the amendment date is not stated in the text.
